pages.text: A LITERAL block holds a fixed value. In its dialog you pick the type and enter the value. The text notation writes them like this:
$(li)$(1)TRUE$() and $(1)FALSE$()$(li)$(1)42$() and $(1)-7$() for integers, $(1)3.14$() for floats$(li)$(1)'a'$() for a CHAR, $(1)"Hello"$() for a STRING$(li)$(1)@2026-10-19T12:05:09Z$() for a TIME

In the dialog, you type a text without quotes. A $(1)"$() in it is just a character. The text notation of the examples puts a backslash in front of it: $(1)"He said \"hi\""$(). $(1)\\$() is a backslash and $(1)\n$() a new line.
